title: Continuous Shot - An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: One take: idea to system
scenes.purpose: A single unbroken camera pull-back and rise turns a close-up of a glowing idea into a high-angle view of a connected system, with no cuts or resets.
visuals: Three.js blue-hour environment: stationary slate-to-navy sky dome, dark tiled ground grid, exponential fog
Warm emissive idea orb on a charcoal plinth acting as the practical light
Five low-saturation extruded blocks (sage, slate blue, mauve, ochre, pale grey) with cream caps
Warm spokes and sage neighbour links drawn as tubes with a leading head
DOM title and corner HUD label in cream

beats.development: Close on the idea orb: it ignites (scale and glow pop) while the camera holds briefly, then starts easing back.
The camera pulls back and rises. Warm spokes shoot from the idea one by one, and each block extrudes from the ground and lights its cap when its spoke arrives.
Sage links close the ring between neighbouring blocks, the hub ring pops, the title fades in and the HUD label changes to SYSTEM as the camera reaches its high angle.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system

beats.development: Settled hold on the complete connected system with the title fully legible.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system

findings: Camera move is one eased curve from 0.15 s to 2.45 s, with no cuts, resets or wall crossings.
Node reveals are staggered 0.13 s apart so the eye follows each spoke to its block.
The title is fully opaque by 2.1 s and every element is settled by 2.45 s, inside the 2.7 s requirement.
justifiedHolds: 0-0.15 s: brief close hold so the viewer finds the idea before the pull-back starts.
2.45-3.0 s: final hold so the title and finished system can be read.

notes: Silent preview: no music, effects or voice.

Palette is a scene-dependent blue-hour alternative to the earlier cream poster. It applies the reviewed split between cool ambient light and a warm practical light, with low-saturation functional block colors on a dark ground.
Blender was not used, at the user's instruction.
